title: GroupBy Aggregations: The Split-Apply-Combine Pattern
code:
import pandas as pd

# Academic departments and student performance
students = pd.DataFrame({
    "Department": ["CS", "Math", "CS", "Physics", "Math", "CS"],
    "Name": ["Arun", "Priya", "Rahul", "Meena", "Kiran", "Divya"],
    "Mark": [85, 92, 78, 88, 95, 90]
})

print("Average Mark per Department:")
print(students.groupby("Department")["Mark"].mean())

print("\nMultiple Aggregations (mean, count, max):")
print(students.groupby("Department")["Mark"].agg(["mean", "count", "max"]))
explanation: df.groupby('Department') splits rows into departmental subsets, applies aggregation functions (.mean(), .agg()) to each subgroup, and combines results into a clean summary table.

title: Custom Data Transformation with apply() and Lambda
code:
import pandas as pd

scores = pd.DataFrame({
    "Student": ["Arun", "Priya", "Rahul", "Meena"],
    "RawScore": [82, 95, 45, 68]
})

# Transform raw score to letter grade using a custom lambda
def assign_grade(score):
    if score >= 90: return "A"
    elif score >= 75: return "B"
    elif score >= 50: return "C"
    else: return "Fail"

scores["Grade"] = scores["RawScore"].apply(assign_grade)
# Also compute a curved score (+5% bonus capped at 100)
scores["Curved"] = scores["RawScore"].apply(lambda s: min(100, round(s * 1.05)))

print("Evaluated Grades with apply():")
print(scores)
explanation: .apply() evaluates custom functions or lambda expressions for every element in a Series, enabling conditional grading and scaling transformations.

title: Sorting DataFrames: Values vs Index
code:
import pandas as pd

products = pd.DataFrame({
    "Item": ["Laptop", "Mouse", "Keyboard", "Monitor"],
    "Price": [55000, 650, 1800, 14500],
    "UnitsSold": [12, 140, 85, 30]
}, index=["P104", "P101", "P103", "P102"])

print("Sorted by Price (Descending):")
print(products.sort_values(by="Price", ascending=False))

print("\nSorted by Index (Ascending):")
print(products.sort_index(ascending=True))
explanation: sort_values(by='Price', ascending=False) ranks rows by numerical value from highest to lowest. sort_index() organizes rows by product code label (P101, P102, ...).

title: Mapping and String Transformations
code:
import pandas as pd

employees = pd.DataFrame({
    "Name": ["  arun kumar ", "priya s", "rahul dev  "],
    "Role": ["E1", "E2", "E1"]
})

# 1. Clean and uppercase text strings with .str accessor
employees["Name"] = employees["Name"].str.strip().str.title()

# 2. Map role codes to official corporate titles
role_titles = {"E1": "Software Engineer", "E2": "Senior Architect"}
employees["Title"] = employees["Role"].map(role_titles)

print("Cleaned and Mapped Employee Table:")
print(employees)
explanation: .str methods (.strip(), .title()) perform vectorized string cleanup. .map(dict) replaces codes with descriptive text based on key matching.
